items.appliesWhen: You wrote a global rule against `.ds-overlay-pane .autocomplete-list` or a sibling. The check icon's `.icon` inside an option is `.option-check` too, and all of them sit inside a new `.dropdown-panel` wrapper. Nothing to do if you only use the `<ds-autocomplete>` element and its inputs.
items.pitfall: The panel is portaled to document.body, so these rules are almost always global rather than component-scoped - grep your global stylesheets, not just the component next to the picker. Retargeting one is also a WIDENING: the three pickers share this panel and it carries no per-picker class, attribute or token, so a rule that used to reach the autocomplete alone now reaches ds-select and ds-multi-select too. There is a second trap under it - a rule of yours on `.ds-overlay-pane` loses to the panel radius and background, which the picker copies off its own host as an inline style. Padding and row-radius compensation in a retargeted rule is dead (delete list: autocomplete-listbox-padding-override).
items.verify: The autocomplete's open panel carries `ds-dropdown-panel` on its `.cdk-overlay-pane`, the panel has 4px padding and its rows a 4px radius without any rule of yours.
items.restore: To keep a rule on one picker, scope it by something outside the pane - a container class on the page - and re-narrow it once a per-picker panel class is available. To set that picker's own radius or background, write it on the host: `ds-autocomplete { --ds-autocomplete-panel-radius: <value>; }`, which is copied onto the pane and wins.
items.note: The panel now renders through the same shared partial as ds-select and ds-multi-select, so it inherits their padding, row radius, selected-row hooks and pressed states. An override that existed only to close that gap is dead weight, and one that names an old class silently stops matching. A `panelClass` input on each picker arrives in 0.13.1 and is the scoped route; until then a widened rule is the only expressible form, so mark it where you write it and narrow it when you reach that version.
items.action: Retarget every rule that names an old class onto its new name.

items.pitfall: The old token painted BOTH the hover and the selected row, because the autocomplete had no separate selected treatment. The panel-level hooks separate them, so a single old value may need splitting across two.
items.verify: A :root or ds-autocomplete override of --ds-option-selected-bg-color repaints the selected row in ds-select and ds-autocomplete. ds-multi-select marks selection with a checkbox, so it answers to --ds-multi-select-check-* instead.
items.note: The autocomplete had no separate selected treatment, so one token painted both hover and selection. The panel-level hooks paint the selected row and its hover in ds-select and ds-autocomplete; ds-multi-select marks selection with a checkbox and answers to --ds-multi-select-check-* instead, and an unselected row's hover is a fixed --surface-secondary with no hook.

items.appliesWhen: You use `<ds-autocomplete>` in single mode in a narrow column.
items.pitfall: Multi mode with the default chip fit is unchanged - its chips already had a measured cap. `maxVisibleChips="all"` is not: the trigger no longer wraps, so its chips stay on one line unless `valueOverflow="wrap"` is set.
items.verify: A long value in a 144px-wide single-select autocomplete keeps the trigger one row tall and ends in an ellipsis, with the full text on the element's title.
items.note: A settled single value now clips with an ellipsis and keeps the trigger one row tall, with the full text on the element title. Multi mode with the default chip fit is untouched - its chips already had a measured cap; with maxVisibleChips="all" the trigger no longer wraps unless valueOverflow="wrap" is set. Nothing in your markup has to change unless the wrapping was deliberate.
items.action: Do nothing, or set valueOverflow="wrap" on the pickers that relied on the value wrapping.

items.appliesWhen: Subclassing a DS component is unsupported, but consumers do it. Template users of the `<ds-…>` elements need nothing.
items.pitfall: `protected` is no protection: a redeclared protected member collides exactly as a public one does. Separately, seventeen symbols are newly exported and can shadow a local name of the same spelling rather than collide with a member: `DsControlWidth`, `DsTriggerDisplay`, `DsChipTemplateDirective`, `DsCreateTemplateDirective`, `DsEmptyTemplateDirective`, `DsOptionTemplateDirective`, `DsPickerTriggerDirective`, `DsOptionGroup`, `DsOptionItem`, `isDsOptionGroup`, `flattenDsOptions`, `AutocompleteItem`, `AutocompleteValueOverflow`, `MultiSelectItem`, `MultiSelectOptionGroup`, `MultiSelectWidth`, `SelectWidth`. Those are new names, not changed ones — nothing of yours breaks unless you already had one. ds-autocomplete also lost the protected computed `filteredGroups`: a subclass member of that name marked `override` fails with TS4113, and one without the modifier compiles and never runs, so check for it by hand.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS2416 naming a picker component.
items.note: All three pickers gained members. ds-select, 5: `width`, `panelTokens`, `optionTemplate`, `emptyTemplate` and `pickerTrigger`. ds-multi-select, 29: `searchable`, `searchableResolved`, `width`, `size`, `sizeResolved`, `triggerDisplay`, `label`, `labelId`, `required`, `optional`, `optionTemplate`, `chipTemplate`, `emptyTemplate`, `pickerTrigger`, `allOptions`, `filteredItems`, `enabledIn`, the private `firstEnabledIndex`, `flatIndexOf`, `isGroup`, `groupAllSelected`, `groupSomeSelected`, `toggleGroup`, `showsCompactTrigger`, `showsGroupSelectAll`, `showsPanelSelectAll`, `showsSearch`, `triggerActiveDescendant` and `triggerCaption`. ds-autocomplete, 16: `valueOverflow`, `label`, `labelId`, `required`, `optional`, `optionTemplate`, `chipTemplate`, `createTemplate`, `emptyTemplate`, `pickerTrigger`, `filteredItems`, `isGroup`, `hasSingleValue`, `selectedOption`, `triggerSelection` and `resolvedAriaLabel`. It lost `optionGroups`, which has its own item, and the protected `filteredGroups`. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported but consumers do it, and a redeclared member collides whether it is public or protected. The compiler enumerates every collision, so a build is the whole check and no list here could stay current.
items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename or mark `override` every member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.

items.pitfall: Only a declaration that re-declares the type structurally (rather than importing it) could notice, and it still sees the same union.
items.verify: The app builds and `width` still accepts only 'fill' and 'content'.
items.note: AutocompleteWidth is now an alias of the shared DsControlWidth that SelectWidth and MultiSelectWidth also alias. The union it resolves to is unchanged, so an import keeps compiling and `width` still accepts exactly `fill` and `content`.

items.action: Move the array you passed to `optionGroups` into `options`.
items.note: The autocomplete took groups in a second input and documented `options` as ignored whenever it was set, so two inputs existed and one silently won. `options` now accepts flat options, groups, or both mixed, in the order given, which is the shape ds-select already used and ds-multi-select has gained.
items.pitfall: If you were passing BOTH inputs and relying on the flat one being dropped, merging them changes what renders — the flat options now appear alongside the groups rather than vanishing.
items.verify: The autocomplete renders its labelled sections with only `options` bound, and filtering still hides a group whose options all fail the query.

items.action: Retarget any rule naming the old classes onto their new names.
items.note: The multi-select carried its own copy of the panel and the option row while its pane also carried ds-dropdown-panel, so both rule sets applied at once and the component’s won. It renders through the shared partial now, like the other two pickers.
items.appliesWhen: You wrote a global rule against `.ds-overlay-pane .panel` or `.options` for the multi-select - both classes live inside its portaled panel.
items.pitfall: The panel is portaled to document.body, so such a rule is almost always global rather than beside the component. A declaration in it that only restored what the shared panel gives - its padding, row radius and fills - restates the default once retargeted.
items.verify: The multi-select panel renders with 4px padding and 4px row radius with no rule of yours, and its rows pick up the shared partial’s hover and active fills.

items.action: Only where you READ the array back or type a variable against its element: change `AutocompleteOption<T>` to `AutocompleteItem<T>` and narrow each element with `isDsOptionGroup` before touching `.value`. Narrow before reading: `for (const item of picker.options()) { if (isDsOptionGroup(item)) continue; /* item.value is safe here */ }`. `isDsOptionGroup` and `flattenDsOptions` are exported from the package root.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that reads the input back, declares a variable or field typed against its element, or overrides a member typed that way. Passing plain options IN is unchanged and needs nothing — a template binding is unaffected.
items.pitfall: The compiler catches the type, not the assumption. Code that already destructures `.value` off each element keeps compiling wherever the variable is inferred rather than annotated, and then reads `undefined` at runtime for a group.
items.note: The element type is now `AutocompleteItem<T>`. The input takes flat options, groups, or both mixed, so an element is no longer always an option.
items.verify: No variable, field or override is typed `AutocompleteOption` where it receives the contents of an `options` array, and every `.value` read off such an element is guarded by `isDsOptionGroup`.

items.action: Only where you READ the array back or type a variable against its element: change `MultiSelectOption` to `MultiSelectItem` and narrow with `isDsOptionGroup` before touching `.value`. Narrow before reading: `for (const item of picker.options()) { if (isDsOptionGroup(item)) continue; /* item.value is safe here */ }`. `isDsOptionGroup` and `flattenDsOptions` are exported from the package root.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that reads the input back, declares a variable or field typed against its element, or overrides a member typed that way. Passing plain options IN is unchanged.
items.pitfall: ds-multi-select accepted no groups at all before this release, so existing code has no reason to guard and every element really was an option. That is exactly why the read sites are worth finding rather than trusting.
items.note: The element type is now `MultiSelectItem`. Groups are new on this component, so the element union is new here too.
items.verify: No variable, field or override is typed `MultiSelectOption` where it receives the contents of an `options` array, and every `.value` read off such an element is guarded by `isDsOptionGroup`.

items.action: Only where you READ `selectAll` back into a `boolean`: widen the receiving type to `boolean | 'group' | 'both'`, or compare against the value you meant (`selectAll() === true`).
items.appliesWhen: Only code that assigns the input back into a `boolean`, or a subclass that re-declares it. Setting it — `[selectAll]="true"` or the bare attribute — is unchanged, and the default is still `false`.
items.pitfall: A truthiness test that used to mean "the whole panel" now also passes for `'group'`, where there is no panel-wide row at all — so a guard written as `if (selectAll())` silently changes meaning while still compiling.
items.note: The type is now `boolean | 'group' | 'both'`. `'group'` renders a row per group and `'both'` adds the panel-wide row beside them.
items.verify: Nothing assigns `selectAll` into a `boolean`, and any truthiness test on it has been read once to confirm it still means what it did.

informational: ds-multi-select and ds-select gained `width`, the input ds-autocomplete already had: `content` takes the trigger width as the panel's floor instead of its width, so a short trigger stops forcing an unreadable panel. Default `fill` is unchanged.
New panel bounds for that mode: --ds-dropdown-panel-minw and --ds-dropdown-panel-maxw.
ds-select now forwards its panel custom properties onto the portaled pane, which it never did — a `ds-select { --ds-dropdown-panel-*: … }` reaches the panel now instead of being silently dropped.
ds-multi-select gained option groups, which it never had. A group disables all of its options when its own `disabled` is set.
ds-multi-select and ds-autocomplete gained `label`, `required` and `optional`, which existed on ds-select alone; ds-multi-select gained `size`, which the other two already had.
New slots: dsEmptyTemplate on all three pickers, dsCreateTemplate on ds-autocomplete. ds-select shows an empty row when it has no options, where it used to open a blank panel.
selectAll on ds-multi-select accepts 'group' and 'both' beside true/false.

All three pickers now forward the four panel-level --ds-option-* hooks onto their portaled pane, so a per-instance override reaches the panel. They paint only ds-select and ds-autocomplete: ds-multi-select marks selection with a checkbox and takes --ds-multi-select-check-* instead.

The dropdown panel geometry now lives only in styles/_dropdown-overlay.scss, behind --ds-dropdown-panel-bg-color/-radius/-maxh/-minw/-maxw. The per-picker names (--ds-multi-select-panel-bg-color, --ds-autocomplete-panel-bg-color/-radius/-maxh) are aliases of those and still work; a global rule of yours that relied on a component stylesheet out-ranking the partial no longer has a competing rule to beat.

ds-multi-select gained `searchable`: true shows the filter row, false hides it, a number sets an option-count threshold. A bare attribute means true. Unset falls back to the new DS_CONFIG.picker.searchable, then true, so nothing changes by default.

deleteList.why: The autocomplete panel shipped with `padding: 0` and square rows while ds-select's dropdown had `--space-1` padding and rounded rows, so consumers patched the difference globally. The panel now uses the same shared partial as the other two pickers and matches without help. Only that compensation is dead: the same rule commonly also carries chrome with no DS equivalent - a border colour, a shadow, a row type scale - and that half is still load-bearing.
deleteList.replaceWith: Nothing for the padding and the row radius - the padding is --space-1 and the row radius is --ds-radius-inner out of the box, and --ds-dropdown-panel-minw / -maxw bound the panel. Keep any declaration in the same rule that is not one of those two, and retarget it onto the new class names.
